s: Who chaired the Fifth Finance Commission (1968)?
x: Mahaveer Tyagi chaired the 5th FC (1968); K.C. Neogy chaired the 1st (1951) and K.C. Pant the 10th (1992).

s: Who chaired the Fourth Finance Commission?
x: P.V. Rajamannar chaired the 4th Finance Commission (1964); A.M. Khusro later chaired the 11th.

s: Who was the chairman of the 16th Finance Commission constituted in 2023?
x: Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th Finance Commission, set up in 2023 for 2026–31. N.K. Singh chaired the 15th and Y.V. Reddy the 14th.

s: Who chaired the Second Finance Commission, constituted in 1956?
x: The 2nd Finance Commission (1956) was chaired by K. Santhanam; A.M. Khusro chaired the 11th (1998) and C. Rangarajan the 12th (2002).

s: Who among the following is a member of the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
x: T. Rabi Sankar is a 16th FC member; Ashok Lahiri and Anoop Singh were in the 15th FC and Sudipto Mundle in the 14th.

s: Who chaired the Third Finance Commission (1960)?
x: A.K. Chanda chaired the 3rd FC (1960); Santhanam chaired the 2nd, Rajamannar the 4th and Tyagi the 5th.

s: Who was the Chairman of the Thirteenth Finance Commission?
x: Vijay L. Kelkar chaired the 13th Finance Commission (award 2010-15).

s: In which year was the First Finance Commission, chaired by K.C. Neogy, constituted?
x: The First Finance Commission under K.C. Neogy was set up in 1951 (order of 22.11.1951); its award covered 1952-57.

s: Who among the following was a member of the Fourteenth Finance Commission?
x: M. Govinda Rao was in the 14th FC; Ramesh Chand and A.N. Jha were 15th FC members and Manoj Panda a 16th FC member.

s: Who chairs the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
x: Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th FC (2026-31); N.K. Singh chaired the 15th and Y.V. Reddy the 14th.

s: Annie George Mathew is a member of which Finance Commission?
x: Annie George Mathew, Manoj Panda and T. Rabi Sankar are members of the 16th FC.

s: Who constitutes the Finance Commission of India?
x: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President every five years under Article 280.

s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Finance Commission under Article 280?
o: Sharing the net proceeds of taxes between the Centre and the States
Recommending principles of grants-in-aid under Article 275
Suggesting measures to augment State Consolidated Funds for local bodies
x: Discretionary grants under Article 282 are not a Finance Commission role; the other three are its duties under Article 280(3).

s: In which year were clauses (bb) and (c) of Article 280(3), on resources for panchayats and municipalities, added?
x: The local-body clauses (bb) and (c) were added in 1992 and rest on State Finance Commission reports.

s: Which of the following lays down the qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission?
o: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003
x: Qualifications are prescribed by the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951.

s: Under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, in which field must the Chairman have experience?
x: The Chairman must have experience in public affairs; judiciary, finance/accounts, administration and economics are fields for the members.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Commission:
1. It is constituted by the President every five years.
2. It consists of a Chairman and four members.
3. Its recommendations are binding on the Union.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The FC is set up by the President every five years with a Chairman and 4 members, but its recommendations are advisory, not binding.

s: Which Article requires the President to lay the report of the Finance Commission before each House of Parliament along with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken?
x: Article 281 requires the President to lay the Finance Commission’s report before each House of Parliament together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken.

s: Through which Constitutional Amendments was the Finance Commission's function of augmenting the Consolidated Fund of a State for Panchayats and Municipalities added?
x: The relevant function was added by the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, 1992, relating respectively to Panchayats and Municipalities.

s: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President every:
x: The quasi-judicial FC is constituted every fifth year or earlier; its recommendations are advisory.

s: Which institution primarily deals with the sharing of GST revenue?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
x: GST revenue-sharing recommendations are dealt with through the GST Council, not as a function of the Finance Commission.

s:
Consider the following about Article 280(3):
1. Clause (b) concerns principles governing grants-in-aid under Article 275.
2. Clause (d) concerns any other matter referred to the Commission by the President.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Article 280(3)(b) covers grants-in-aid principles under Article 275, and clause (d) any other matter referred by the President.

s: What is the nature of the recommendations of the Finance Commission?
o: Binding on the Union and the States
Advisory and not binding on the Government
x: FC recommendations are not binding on the Government; it may also deal with matters referred by the President.

s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Finance Commission under Article 280?
o: Sharing net tax proceeds between the Centre and the States
Principles of grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of India
Measures to augment State Consolidated Funds for Panchayats
Maintaining income-expenditure accounts of the Union and the States
x: Keeping the accounts of the Union and States is not an FC duty; the other three are under Article 280(3).

s: What kind of body is the Finance Commission of India?
x: The Finance Commission is a constitutional, quasi-judicial body formed by the President under Article 280.

s: On whose recommendations does the Central Finance Commission suggest measures under Article 280(3)(bb) and (c) to augment the State Consolidated Fund for local bodies?
x: The Central Finance Commission makes such recommendations on the basis of State Finance Commission recommendations.

s: To what level did the Fourteenth Finance Commission raise the States' share in the divisible pool?
x: The 14th FC raised the share from 32% to 42%, a rise of 10 points; the 15th set 41%.

s: What share of the divisible pool did the Thirteenth Finance Commission recommend for the States?
x: The 13th FC fixed the States' share at 32%; the 14th raised it to 42%.

s: What weight did income distance carry under the Fourteenth Finance Commission?
x: The 14th FC gave 50% to income distance, 17.5% to 1971 population, 10% to 2011 population and 15% to area.

s: Which distinction was ended by the Fourteenth Finance Commission?
x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission ended the distinction between Plan and non-Plan expenditure.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Fourteenth Finance Commission is correctly matched?
o: Main route of transfers – Tax devolution
Distinction ended – Tied and untied grants
Distinction ended – Central and State taxes
x: The 14th FC made tax devolution, rather than grants, the main route of transfers; the distinction it ended was between Plan and non-Plan expenditure.

s: Which Finance Commission made no distinction between general and Special Category States in tax sharing?
x: The 14th FC made no distinction between general and Special Category States in sharing.

s: Under the Fourteenth Finance Commission's fiscal roadmap, at what level was the fiscal deficit of States anchored?
x: The 14th FC roadmap set the Centre's fiscal deficit at 3% of GDP and anchored the States' at 3% of GSDP.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Fourteenth Finance Commission:
1. It made tax devolution, not grants, the main route of transfers.
2. It excluded States from NSSF loans from 2015-16.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 14th FC made devolution the main route and excluded States from NSSF loans from 2015-16, so both are correct.

s: How much grant to gram panchayats did the Fourteenth Finance Commission recommend for 2015-20?
x: The 14th FC gave gram panchayats about ₹2.00 lakh crore; ₹2.36 lakh crore was the 15th FC's rural grant.

s: Under which Finance Commission did the largest-ever increase in the States' share of Union taxes occur?
x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission increased the States' share from 32 per cent to 42 per cent, a rise of 10 percentage points, the largest-ever jump.

s: Who was the Chairman of the Fifteenth Finance Commission?
x: N.K. Singh chaired the 15th Finance Commission (2020-21 and 2021-26).

s: When was the Fifteenth Finance Commission constituted?
x: The 15th FC under N.K. Singh was set up on 27 November 2017; the 14th on 2 January 2013.

s: Which period did the awards of the Fifteenth Finance Commission cover?
x: The 15th FC gave an interim report for 2020-21 and a main report for 2021-26.

s: Which of the following pairs of criterion and weight under the Fifteenth Finance Commission is correctly matched?
o: Forest cover and ecology — 2.5 per cent
x: Under the Fifteenth Finance Commission, income distance carried 45 per cent. Population of 2011, forest cover and ecology, and demographic performance carried 15, 10 and 12.5 per cent respectively.

s: How much did the Fifteenth Finance Commission provide as grants for Rural Local Bodies?
x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission provided ₹2.36 lakh crore for Rural Local Bodies during 2021–26. The Fourteenth Finance Commission gave gram panchayats about ₹2.00 lakh crore.

s: For what did the Fifteenth Finance Commission recommend ₹4,800 crore for 2022-23 to 2025-26 to incentivise States?
x: An amount of ₹4,800 crore was recommended to incentivise States on educational outcomes during 2022–23 to 2025–26.

s: The 15th Finance Commission was mandated to use the population data of which Census?
x: Its terms of reference required 2011 population data, and also covered disaster-management financing and a non-lapsable defence fund.

s: Besides the use of Census 2011, the 15th Finance Commission's terms of reference covered a non-lapsable fund for which sector?
x: The 15th FC's ToR included a non-lapsable defence fund along with disaster funding.

s: Which States mainly objected to the use of 2011 Census population by the 15th Finance Commission?
x: Southern States objected to the 15th FC being told to use the 2011 Census.

s: Why was the States' share reduced from 42% under the 14th Finance Commission to 41% under the 15th Finance Commission?
o: The abolition of the divisible pool
The introduction of the GDP criterion
Jammu and Kashmir becoming a Union Territory
x: The reduction was attributed to Jammu and Kashmir becoming a Union Territory.

s: Which matter was referred by the President to the Fifteenth Finance Commission under Article 280(3)(d)?
o: Disaster financing under the Disaster Management Act, 2005
x: Clause (d) covers any matter the President refers, such as disaster financing under the DM Act, 2005 for the 15th FC.

s: In which area did the 15th Finance Commission recommend ₹4,800 crore for 2022-23 to 2025-26 to incentivise States?
x: The 15th FC set aside Rs 4,800 crore (2022-23 to 2025-26) to reward States for better educational outcomes (UPSC 2025). Property tax was an entry condition for local-body grants, power-sector reform was tied to extra borrowing, and disaster funds come through SDRF/SDMF.

s: Under which provision was the award of the Thirteenth Finance Commission to undivided Andhra Pradesh apportioned between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
o: Section 46(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014
x: Section 46(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided for apportionment using population ratio and other parameters.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Finance Commission grants and Andhra Pradesh?
o: 15th FC grants for 2024-25 and 2025-26 were drawn in advance by the previous government
AP's revenue deficit during 2014-19 was ₹48,000 crore
AP said it could lose up to ₹38,000 crore after the 16th FC dropped special grants
AP's projected revenue deficit for 2025-26 was ₹48,000 crore
x: AP's revenue deficit during 2014-19 was ₹16,000 crore; ₹48,000 crore was the projected revenue deficit for 2025-26.

s: Post-bifurcation Andhra Pradesh depended substantially on which of the following sources for meeting its fiscal and disaster-related requirements?
o: 15th and 16th Finance Commission special category grants only
14th and 15th Finance Commission revenue deficit grants and disaster funds
Central plan assistance under the 12th Finance Commission
x: Post-bifurcation Andhra Pradesh depended heavily on the revenue deficit grants and disaster funds provided through the 14th and 15th Finance Commissions.

s: How much was the revenue deficit grant to Andhra Pradesh under the 14th Finance Commission (2015-20)?
x: AP got about ₹22,113 crore as 14th FC revenue deficit grant; ₹16,000 crore was its 2014-19 revenue deficit.

s: In lieu of which of the following was Andhra Pradesh given a special package?
x: The special package to AP was given in lieu of Special Category Status.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's share in horizontal devolution under the 16th Finance Commission?
x: The 16th FC raised AP's share to 4.217% from 4.047% under the 15th FC.

s: What is the award period of the 16th Finance Commission?
x: The 16th Finance Commission covers 2026–27 to 2030–31.

s: On which date was the Sixteenth Finance Commission constituted?
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023. Its report was tabled on 1 February 2026.

s: What share of the divisible pool did the States demand from the Sixteenth Finance Commission, a demand it rejected?
x: The 16th FC retained 41% and rejected the demand for 50%.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the devolution criteria of the 16th Finance Commission?
o: The tax and fiscal effort criterion was dropped
The weight of income distance was reduced to 42.5%
Contribution to GDP was added with a 10% weight
x: The 16th FC cut the weight of area to 10%.

s: To what level did the 16th Finance Commission raise the weight of population?
x: Population weight was raised to 17.5% and a GDP criterion was added; all five southern States saw their shares rise.

s: Which horizontal devolution criterion of the 15th Finance Commission was dropped by the 16th Finance Commission?
x: Tax/fiscal effort (2.5% under the 15th FC) was dropped by the 16th FC; area, forest and demographic performance were retained at 10% each.

s: To what level did the Sixteenth Finance Commission cut the weight of area in horizontal devolution from 15%?
x: Area weight fell from 15% (14th and 15th FC) to 10% under the 16th FC.

s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission, what happened to the shares of the five southern States in tax devolution?
x: Under the 16th Finance Commission the shares of all five southern States in tax devolution rose.

s: How much do local bodies receive as grants under the 16th Finance Commission?
x: Of total grants of ₹9.47 lakh crore, local bodies get ₹7.91 lakh crore (rural 4.35, urban 3.56).

s: Under the 16th Finance Commission's disaster-funding framework, what is the Centre-State cost-sharing ratio for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and for other States, respectively?
x: North-Eastern and Himalayan States share disaster funding 90:10 with the Centre; all other States share it 75:25. A reverses the two, and B and D give ratios the Commission did not recommend.

s: From which date did the Sixteenth Finance Commission's recommendations come into force?
x: The 16th FC report was submitted on 17 Nov 2025, tabled on 1 Feb 2026 and came into force on 1 Apr 2026.

s: What is the total amount of grants recommended by the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
x: The 16th FC recommended total grants of ₹9.47 lakh crore, of which ₹7.91 lakh crore is for local bodies.

s: On which date was the report of the Sixteenth Finance Commission tabled in Parliament?
x: The report was submitted on 17 November 2025, tabled on 1 February 2026 and came into force on 1 April 2026.

s: Which was the first Finance Commission to use contribution to GDP as a criterion of devolution?
x: The 16th FC, the present Commission, was the first to use contribution to GDP (10% weight).

s: At what level did the 16th Finance Commission retain the States' share in the divisible pool?
x: It retained 41 per cent; the demand of 18 of 28 States for 50 per cent was not accepted.

s: Which Finance Commission recommended the National Disaster Reserve Fund?
x:
Most keys: 11th FC for the 'National Disaster Reserve Fund'. Strictly, the fund was the National Calamity Contingency Fund (Arthapedia, ies.gov.in).
The 11th Finance Commission recommended the National Calamity Contingency Fund (₹500 crore corpus; renamed National Disaster Response Fund in 2010) – the fund such questions mean by a 'National Disaster Reserve Fund'. No separate 'reserve fund supplementing the NCCF' existed.

s: In the context of fiscal federalism in India, what does vertical devolution refer to?
o: allocation of grants among local bodies
sharing of net tax proceeds between the Union and the States
distribution of the States' share among individual States
distribution of centrally sponsored schemes among districts
x: Vertical devolution means sharing net tax proceeds between the Union and the States. Distribution of the States' share among individual States is horizontal devolution.

s: What were the States' shares of central taxes recommended by the 10th to 13th Finance Commissions?
x: The respective shares were 29% under the 10th, 29.5% under the 11th, 30.5% under the 12th and 32% under the 13th Finance Commission.

s: The 80th Constitutional Amendment, 2000 gave effect to the 'Alternative Scheme of Devolution' of which Finance Commission?
x: The 80th Amendment implemented the 10th FC's Alternative Scheme (29%), making all central taxes shareable with effect from 1 April 1996.

s: From which date did the 80th Constitutional Amendment, making all central taxes shareable, take effect?
x: The 80th Amendment (2000) took effect retrospectively from 1 April 1996.

s: How many of the 28 States sought a 50% share of the divisible pool from the 16th Finance Commission?
x: 18 of 28 States sought 50%; the 16th FC rejected it and retained 41%.

s: Which of the following was NOT a basis of the Fourteenth Finance Commission's recommendation on the States' vertical share?
o: Fiscal space of the Centre and the States
x: The 14th FC based the vertical share on constitutional spirit, fiscal space and clarity of functions, not on aspirations of State populations.

s: Which State got the largest share of tax devolution under the Fourteenth Finance Commission, at about 17.96%?
x: Uttar Pradesh, the most populous State, got the biggest slice (about 17.96%) under the 14th FC.

s: Under the 16th Finance Commission award, to what level did Andhra Pradesh's share rise from about 4.047 per cent?
x: Andhra Pradesh’s share increased from 4.047 per cent to 4.217 per cent under the 16th Finance Commission. It is also rounded as 4.22 per cent and 4.05 per cent in some presentations.

s: What was the principal shift associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission in intergovernmental transfers?
o: From performance-based transfers to unconditional entitlement
From tax devolution to complete abolition of grants
From State transfers to exclusive Central expenditure
From entitlement-based transfers to performance-oriented transfers
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission is associated with a shift from entitlement-based transfers towards performance-oriented transfers.

s: Which of the following best reflects the equity-efficiency issue in the design of fiscal devolution?
o: All States possess identical fiscal capacity, so devolution automatically equalises them.
Most Finance Commissions relied on income distance and population, while critics argue that fiscal capacity is not uniform.
Efficiency requires replacing all tax devolution with discretionary grants.
Equity is achieved only when every State receives an identical absolute amount.
x: Most Finance Commissions relied on income distance and population to pursue equity. Critics argue that fiscal capacity is not uniform, so devolution is not automatically self-equalising.

s: What weight did the 16th Finance Commission give to 'contribution to GDP'?
x: GDP contribution got a 10% weight, criticised for rewarding size rather than need; the tax-effort criterion (2.5% under the 15th FC) was dropped.

s: What weight was given to 1971 population under the 14th Finance Commission?
x: The 14th FC gave 17.5% to 1971 population and 10% to 2011 population.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's share in horizontal devolution under the 14th Finance Commission?
x: AP's share was 4.305% under the 14th FC, 4.047% under the 15th (2021-26) and 4.217% under the 16th.

s: Which State has the largest share in horizontal devolution under the Fifteenth Finance Commission?
x: Uttar Pradesh has the largest share (about 17.9%) under the 15th FC; Bihar comes second.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's share in horizontal devolution under the Fifteenth Finance Commission for 2021-26?
x: AP's share was 4.305% under the 14th FC, 4.111% (2020-21) and 4.047% (2021-26) under the 15th FC, and 4.217% under the 16th.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sixteenth Finance Commission's disaster funding?
o: It recommended disaster grants of ₹1.55 lakh crore
It proposed a State disaster corpus of ₹2.04 lakh crore
It added heatwaves and lightning as notified disasters
x: The 16th FC did not discontinue disaster grants; it recommended ₹1.55 lakh crore for them and added heatwaves and lightning as notified disasters.

s: Which of the following grants was NOT recommended by the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
x: The 16th FC gave only local body and disaster grants and recommended no revenue deficit grants.

s: For which of the following are Article 275 grants NOT generally meant?
o: Welfare of Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas
x: Article 275 grants support revenue deficits, local bodies, disasters and tribal welfare, not every CSS.

s: Which approach was associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission’s treatment of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
o: Linking them to measurable outcomes and reviewing inefficient schemes
Charging all CSS directly to the Consolidated Fund of India as Article 275 grants
Transferring their administration exclusively to local bodies
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission linked CSS to measurable outcomes and proposed a high-powered committee to close inefficient schemes.

s: Which of the following Centre-to-State transfers is untied?
x: Tax devolution under Article 270 is untied; Article 282 grants are discretionary and CSS generally need a matching State share.

s: Centrally Sponsored Schemes are best described as schemes which are
o: recommended only by the Finance Commission and funded only from Article 275 grants
designed by States and financed entirely by local bodies
designed by the Centre and require a matching State share
implemented without any State financial contribution
x: Centrally Sponsored Schemes are Centre-designed schemes requiring a matching contribution from the States.

s: Which of the following grants were discontinued by the 16th Finance Commission?
o: Revenue-deficit grants, sector-specific grants and State-specific grants
All grants to rural local bodies
x: The 16th Finance Commission discontinued revenue-deficit grants, sector-specific grants and State-specific grants.

s: Tax devolution from the Centre to the States takes place under which Article?
x: Tax devolution is under Article 270; Article 275 covers FC grants, Article 282 CSS and other transfers, and Article 123 is the ordinance power.

s: What is the general nature of grants under Article 282?
o: Statutory grants recommended by the Finance Commission
Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Discretionary, mostly tied and routed through Union ministries
Untied transfers from the divisible pool
x: Article 282 grants are discretionary, mostly tied and scheme-based; Article 275 grants are statutory and charged on the CFI.

s: About how much did the 15th Finance Commission's revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants total?
x: The 15th FC's grants totalled about ₹10.1 lakh crore, against ₹9.47 lakh crore under the 16th FC.

s: Which two phenomena were recommended to be notified as disasters under the disaster-grant framework?
x: Heatwave and lightning were recommended to be notified as disasters.

s: Which body releases central transfers to the States?
x: The Union Finance Ministry releases transfers to States; NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation role.

s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission, the share of grants in total Finance Commission transfers fell from 19.4% to about what level?
x: The 16th FC cut grants to local body and disaster grants only, so their share fell from 19.4% to 8.3%.

s: What is the allocation for Centrally Sponsored Schemes in the Union Budget 2026-27?
x: CSS allocation for 2026-27 is ₹5,48,798 crore, up 30.6%.

s: What was the principal effect attributed to SASCI in the Economic Survey analysis?
o: It restricted capital expenditure to higher-income States.
It reduced State capital expenditure by replacing grants with revenue loans.
It converted all State borrowings into tax devolution.
It helped prevent pro-cyclical compression of State capital expenditure through 50-year interest-free capex loans.
x: SASCI provides 50-year interest-free capital expenditure loans and helped prevent pro-cyclical compression of State capital expenditure.

s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission framework, at what level should the fiscal deficit of a State be capped?
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended capping State fiscal deficits at 3% of GSDP.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2016-17, redistributive transfers had a suggestive negative effect on which of the following for States?
x: ES 2016-17 found a suggestive negative effect on own tax effort and no positive link with consumption, growth or governance.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Economic Survey 2016-17 findings on redistributive transfers?
o: No positive link with per capita consumption
No positive link with GSDP growth
Transfers should be linked to fiscal and governance effort
x: ES 2016-17 found no positive link with governance, consumption or GSDP growth, and suggested linking transfers to effort.

s: States were allowed extra borrowing of 0.5% of GSDP linked to reforms in which sector?
x: An extra 0.5% of GSDP was allowed for power-sector reforms (2021-22 to 2024-25, again 2025-26).

s: The unused GST compensation cess is split 50:50 between the Centre and the States. In proportion to what is the States' half shared among them?
x: The unused balance is shared among States by SGST revenue, not population.

s: GST compensation to States was paid for five years from July 2017. In which month did it end?
x: Compensation was paid July 2017 – June 2022; the cess continued to repay COVID loans and ended on 22 Sep 2025 except for tobacco.

s: States were allowed extra borrowing equal to their contributions to which of the following?
x: States may borrow extra equal to their NPS/UPS contributions (₹62,778 crore in 2024-25).

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, State capital expenditure rose from 2.17% of GDP in FY22 to what level in FY25?
x: The Survey credits SASCI loans for raising State capex from 2.17% (FY22) to 2.37% of GDP (FY25).

s: How much is the devolution of taxes to the States in the Union Budget 2026-27?
x: Budget 2026-27 puts tax devolution at ₹15,26,255 crore within total transfers of ₹26,20,769 crore.

s: What does the expression '41% illusion' in discussions on tax devolution refer to?
o: cesses and surcharges are outside the divisible pool
the Finance Commission fixes all tax rates at 41%
States receive 41% of total public expenditure
41% of the divisible pool is transferred only through grants
x: The expression highlights that the stated share can overstate actual resources available to States because growing cesses and surcharges remain outside the divisible pool.

s: Which of the following is excluded from the divisible pool of Union taxes?
x: Cesses and surcharges are excluded from the divisible pool, as is the cost of collection; pool taxes are shared under Article 270.

s:
Consider the following about the divisible pool of central taxes:
1. It excludes cesses and surcharges.
2. It was about 81% of gross tax revenue in 2025–26.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The divisible pool comprises shareable taxes under Article 270, excluding cesses and surcharges, and was about 81% of gross tax revenue in 2025–26.

s: The divisible pool as a share of gross tax revenue fell from 89.2% in the 13th FC period to about what level in the 15th FC period?
x: The pool fell from 89.2% (FC-13) to 82.1% (FC-14) and 78.3% (FC-15) as cesses and surcharges rose.

s: What did the Sixteenth Finance Commission recommend to improve transparency about the divisible pool?
o: Merging the GST Council with the Finance Commission
Annual CAG-certified disclosure of net tax proceeds
x: The 16th FC asked for an annual CAG-certified statement of net tax proceeds; it said capping cesses was not permissible.

s: Under the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula, which pair of criterion and weight is correctly matched?
x: Population carried 60%, per capita income 25%, tax effort 7.5% and special problems 7.5%.

s: In which year was the Gadgil formula introduced?
x: The Gadgil formula dates to 1969; formula-based plan transfers lapsed when NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.

s: Which of the following was among the initial Special Category States under the Gadgil formula?
x: The initial Special Category States were Assam, Jammu and Kashmir, and Nagaland.

s: Under the Gadgil formula, central plan assistance to Special Category States and to general-category States was given in which grant-loan proportions, respectively?
x: Special Category States received assistance as 90% grant and 10% loan; general-category States received 30% grant and 70% loan. D reverses the two, and B and C are not the Gadgil proportions.

s: In which year did formula-based plan transfers end, when NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission?
x: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015, ending Gadgil-Mukherjee formula transfers.

s: Which body endorsed the Gadgil formula in 1968-69?
x: The National Development Council endorsed the Gadgil formula in 1968-69; it was used from the Fourth Plan (1969).

s: Which of the following criteria was used in the Gadgil formula (1969) but dropped in the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula (1991)?
x: Gadgil gave 10% to ongoing irrigation and power projects; Gadgil-Mukherjee dropped it.

s: What weight did the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula give to per capita income?
x: Gadgil-Mukherjee: population 60%, per capita income 25%, tax effort 7.5%, special problems 7.5%.

s: Which is the largest component of central transfers to Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26 (RE)?
x: FC grants are AP's largest central transfer: ₹62,188 crore of ₹1,04,493 crore (2025-26 RE).

s: About how much is the 16th Finance Commission's grant to Andhra Pradesh's rural local bodies?
x: AP gets ₹16,627 crore for rural LBs, ₹12,158 crore for urban LBs and ₹6,125 crore for disasters.

s: How much disaster grant does the Sixteenth Finance Commission give Andhra Pradesh?
x: 16th FC grants to AP: rural local bodies ₹16,627 crore, urban ₹12,158 crore, disaster ₹6,125 crore.

s: After the loss of the revenue deficit grant, what is Andhra Pradesh's revenue deficit in Budget 2026-27?
x: With the 16th FC ending revenue deficit grants, AP's revenue deficit is 1.1% in Budget 2026-27.

s: What is the tied portion of the 15th Finance Commission's grants to rural local bodies?
x: 60% is tied (drinking water, rainwater harvesting, sanitation) and 40% untied.

s: For which of the following can the untied grants to rural local bodies under the 15th Finance Commission NOT be used?
x: The 40% untied part is for local needs but not for salaries.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 15th Finance Commission's rural local body grants:
1. Provisional and audited accounts must be in the public domain for at least 25% of rural local bodies.
2. Constitution of the State Finance Commission is mandatory for release from 2024-25.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are release conditions: accounts in the public domain for at least 25% of rural local bodies, and an SFC from 2024-25.

s:
Consider the following statements about entry conditions for local bodies under the 16th Finance Commission:
1. Audited accounts must be published online.
2. Issue of municipal bonds is mandatory.
3. The State Finance Commission must be constituted on time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The entry conditions are elected bodies, online audited accounts and timely SFCs; issuing municipal bonds is not a condition.

s: What share of the 16th Finance Commission's local-body grants does the basic grant form?
x: The basic grant is 80% (half tied, half untied); the 20% performance grant is fully untied.

s: With which of the following is the one-time Urbanisation Premium associated?
o: Merging peri-urban villages under a Rural-to-Urban Transition Policy
x: The premium is tied to merging peri-urban villages and adopting a Rural-to-Urban Transition Policy.

s: To what level did the urban share in the Sixteenth Finance Commission's local-body grants rise from 36%?
x: The urban share increased from 36% to 45%. The projected urbanisation level by 2031 was 41%, which is a separate figure.

s: Which was an entry condition for urban local bodies to receive the relevant Fifteenth Finance Commission grants?
o: Publication of audited accounts and notification of baseline property-tax rates
Transfer of land-revenue powers to municipalities
Issue of municipal bonds by every town
Levy of professional tax at the maximum permitted rate
x: ULBs had to publish audited accounts and notify baseline property-tax rates to become eligible for the grants.

s: What is the nature of the performance grant under the 16th Finance Commission's local-body grants?
x: The performance grant (20%) is fully untied; the basic grant (80%) is half tied and half untied.

s: How much special infrastructure grant did the Sixteenth Finance Commission give urban local bodies for wastewater in cities of 10-40 lakh population?
x: The special infrastructure component is ₹56,100 crore; the Urbanisation Premium is ₹10,000 crore.

s: What is the size of the one-time Urbanisation Premium under the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
x: The Urbanisation Premium is a one-time ₹10,000 crore for merging peri-urban villages into cities.

s: About how much did the Fifteenth Finance Commission give local bodies as grants?
x: Local-body grants rose from about ₹4.36 lakh crore (15th FC) to ₹7,91,493 crore (16th FC).

s:
Consider the following statements about the 16th Finance Commission's basic grant to local bodies:
1. Half of it is tied to water and sanitation.
2. It is fully untied.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The basic grant (80%) is half tied (water, sanitation) and half untied; the performance grant (20%) is fully untied.

s: Gram panchayats may levy which of the following, subject to authorisation by the State?
x: Gram panchayats levy only State-authorised taxes, including taxes on local fairs, house or property tax, fees and tolls. Sales tax and land revenue are State levies.

s: Being constrained in their power to tax, on which of the following do panchayats substantially depend?
x: Panchayats depend substantially on grants; gram sabhas spend only about 4% of their time on revenue generation.

s: Which of the following is NOT a direct source of funds for Panchayats?
x: Panchayats get FC grants, SFC allocations, CSS funds and loans from Central Cooperative Banks; NABARD is not a direct source.

s:
Consider the following statements about State Finance Commissions:
1. There is no separate State Finance Commission for Municipalities.
2. The State Finance Commission constituted under Article 243I also reviews municipal finances under Article 243Y.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the same SFC constituted by the Governor under Article 243I reviews municipal finances under Article 243Y, so no separate SFC exists.

s: What does the word 'may' in Article 243H indicate?
o: The State Legislature has an enabling power and is not compelled to impose the taxes
Only the Union Parliament can authorise local taxation
Panchayats can impose taxes without State authorisation
The State Legislature is constitutionally compelled to impose every listed tax
x: The use of ‘may’ makes the provision enabling rather than compulsory; the State Legislature may authorise the levy, collection and appropriation of the listed revenues.

s: Under Article 243I, who constitutes the State Finance Commission for panchayats?
x: The Governor constitutes the SFC every five years under Article 243I.

s: How many subjects are listed in the Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution?
x: The Eleventh Schedule (Art. 243G) lists 29 subjects; the Twelfth (Art. 243W) lists 18.

s: The Twelfth Schedule, listing 18 subjects for municipalities, is linked to which Article?
x: The Twelfth Schedule goes with Article 243W; the Eleventh goes with Article 243G.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: 243H and 243I concern Panchayats; 243X and 243Y concern Municipalities.

s: Under Article 243I, after how many years is a State Finance Commission constituted?
x: The Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission every five years under Article 243I.

s: In the decentralisation debate, what do the '3Fs' that rarely move together to local bodies refer to?
x: The Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules are only enabling, so funds, functions and functionaries rarely move together.

s: Who chaired Andhra Pradesh's Fifth State Finance Commission?
x: Prof. S. Rathna Kumari chaired the 5th SFC; Prof. G. Nancharaiah chaired the 4th.

s: Which period does the report of Andhra Pradesh's Fifth State Finance Commission (31 Dec 2024) cover?
x: The 5th SFC reported on 31 Dec 2024 for 2025-30.

s:
Consider the following statements about State Finance Commissions in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The SFC consists of a chairman and four members.
2. Its members are appointed by the Chief Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AP's SFC has a chairman and 4 members, but they are appointed by the Governor, not the Chief Minister.

s: Who chaired Andhra Pradesh's Fourth State Finance Commission?
x: Prof. G. Nancharaiah chaired AP's 4th SFC, which reported on 30 October 2019.

s: In which cities did the Economic Survey 2016-17 use satellite imagery to estimate the gap between actual and potential property tax?
x: The Economic Survey 2016-17 measured the actual-potential property-tax gap in Bengaluru and Jaipur using satellite imagery.

s: Chronic under-assessment and under-collection of which tax mainly explains the weak revenue position of municipalities?
x: Municipal finances are weakened particularly by chronic under-assessment and under-collection of property tax.

s: Which of the following is a non-tax revenue source of urban local bodies?
x: Rents, fees and fines are non-tax revenues; professional and advertisement taxes are tax revenues.

s: Drone maps under which scheme can give panchayats a property-tax baseline?
x: SVAMITVA drone maps provide a property-tax baseline; AMRUT 2.0 incentivises property-tax reform and municipal bonds.

s: What is the ceiling on professional tax levied by local bodies?
x: Professional tax is a tax source of ULBs with a ceiling of ₹2,500.

s: Which is the most important own tax source of urban local bodies?
x: Property tax is the most important own tax of municipalities, though it is under-assessed and under-collected.

s: Which mission rewards cities for property-tax reform and municipal bonds?
x: AMRUT 2.0 rewards property-tax reform and municipal bonds; SVAMITVA gives drone maps for panchayats.

s: Which of the following committees is correctly matched with its period and chairperson?
o: Local Finance Enquiry Committee (1949-51) – P.K. Wattal
Committee on Panchayati Raj Finances (1963) – John Matthai
x: The Local Finance Enquiry Committee (1949-51) was headed by P.K. Wattal. John Matthai chaired the Taxation Enquiry Commission, K. Santhanam the Committee on Panchayati Raj Finances and A.P. Jain the Rural-Urban Relationship Committee.

s: Who chaired the National Commission on Urbanisation (1985-88)?
x: The National Commission on Urbanisation functioned during 1985-88 under the chairmanship of Charles Correa.

s: Who chaired the Taxation Enquiry Commission (1953-54)?
x: John Matthai chaired the Taxation Enquiry Commission; A.P. Jain chaired the Rural-Urban Relationship Committee (1963-66).

s: Who chaired the Rural-Urban Relationship Committee (1963-66)?
x: The Rural-Urban Relationship Committee (1963-66) was chaired by A.P. Jain.

s: Who chaired the Committee on Panchayati Raj Finances (1963)?
x: K. Santhanam headed the 1963 committee on Panchayati Raj finances.

s: Which of the following is identified as a barrier to local bodies’ access to the bond market?
o: Excessive accrual accounting and strong balance sheets
Absence of accrual accounting and weak balance sheets
Complete dependence on property tax surpluses
Excessive control over State line-department staff
x: The absence of accrual accounting and weak balance sheets restrict local bodies’ access to the bond market.

s: According to the IIHS study covering 80 urban local bodies during 2012–17, intergovernmental transfers accounted for approximately what share of ULB revenue?
x: The IIHS study reported that intergovernmental transfers constituted about 40 percent of ULB revenue.

s: What are India's intergovernmental transfers as a share of GDP and the global norm, respectively?
x: India's intergovernmental transfers are about 0.5% of GDP, compared with a global norm of roughly 2–5% of GDP.

s: Delayed local-body elections in Andhra Pradesh put Finance Commission grants at risk. To which of the following are these grants linked?
o: Access of municipalities to the bond market
Appointment of Special Officers to run the bodies
Elected bodies, audited accounts and compliance with State Finance Commission requirements
x: The grants are tied to the existence of elected bodies, audited accounts and SFC compliance, so delayed elections jeopardise eligibility and release.

s: By whom were Andhra Pradesh's local bodies run after their terms ended in 2026?
x: ULB terms ended 15 March 2026 and panchayat terms 4 April 2026, so Special Officers took charge, putting FC grants at risk.

s: About how much is the 16th Finance Commission's grant to Andhra Pradesh's urban local bodies?
x: AP's urban LBs get ₹12,158 crore and rural LBs ₹16,627 crore under the 16th FC.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the shares of Union Budget 2026-27 expenditure?
o: States' share of taxes is the largest item at 22 per cent
Central Sector Schemes take 17 per cent
Defence takes a larger share than interest
x: Defence takes 11 per cent, well below interest at 20 per cent. The order is States' share of taxes 22, interest 20, Central Sector Schemes 17 and defence 11 per cent.

s: Interest payments in Union Budget Estimates 2026-27 were approximately what proportion of total expenditure and revenue receipts, respectively?
x: Interest payments of ₹14,03,972 crore represented 26 per cent of total expenditure and 40 per cent of revenue receipts.

s: What proportion of revenue receipts did committed expenditure on salaries, pensions and interest payments account for?
x: Committed expenditure, comprising salaries, pensions and interest payments, was 65.3 per cent of revenue receipts.

s: Union total expenditure in Budget Estimates 2026-27 is about what share of GDP?
x: Total expenditure of ₹53,47,315 crore is 13.6 per cent of GDP; revenue expenditure alone is 10.5 per cent.

s: In Union Budget 2023-24, major subsidies took what share of every rupee spent?
x: Major subsidies took 7 per cent in 2023-24 BE (6 per cent in 2026-27); 9 per cent is a common wrong figure.

s: The share of revenue expenditure in total Union expenditure fell from 88% in 2014-15 to about what level by 2026-27?
x: Revenue expenditure fell from 88% (2014-15) to about 77% of the total as capital spending rose.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Item)
A. Interest payments
B. Education
C. Loans to States
D. Grants to States
List-II (Classification)
1. Capital expenditure
2. Non-developmental expenditure
3. Revenue expenditure even if assets are created
4. Developmental expenditure
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Interest is non-developmental, education is developmental, loans to States are capital and grants to States are revenue.

s: Under which head are loans and advances given by the Union Government to States classified?
x: Loans and advances to States change the Government's financial assets, so they are capital expenditure. Maintenance of assets and interest payments are revenue expenditure.

s: How is government expenditure that creates an asset or reduces a liability classified?
x: Capital expenditure either creates assets or reduces liabilities; revenue expenditure generally does neither.

s: Under which head are subsidies ordinarily classified?
x: Subsidies are revenue expenditure; grants to States are also revenue expenditure, while defence equipment purchase can be capital outlay.

s: According to the 'Golden Rule' of public finance, for what should government borrowing ordinarily be used?
o: Creation of assets through capital expenditure
x: The Golden Rule allows borrowing only for asset creation, so the quality and composition of spending matter more than its size.

s: Why does capital expenditure strengthen long-term productive capacity?
o: Meets the recurring running costs of government
Is directed at acquiring, creating, upgrading or extending the life of assets
Covers salaries, pensions and interest payments
Is given as grants to States for their schemes
x: Capital spending buys, creates, upgrades or extends the life of assets, which builds long-term capacity. Running costs, salaries, interest and grants to States are revenue expenditure.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Capital expenditure – directed toward creation or acquisition of assets
Non-plan expenditure – included subsidies, interest payments and defence
Revenue expenditure – involves no creation of assets
Revenue deficit – revenue receipts minus revenue expenditure
x: Revenue deficit is revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts, not the reverse.

s: How are grants given by the Union to States classified, even when they are used to create assets?
x: Grants to States are revenue expenditure even if assets are made; loans to States are capital expenditure.

s:
Consider the following statements about expenditure classification:
1. Food and fertiliser subsidies are revenue expenditure.
2. Repayment of loans is revenue expenditure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Subsidies are revenue expenditure. Repayment of loans reduces a liability, so it is capital expenditure.

s: Under which head is the purchase of defence equipment classified in the Union Budget?
x: Defence equipment is capital outlay, so it is capital expenditure, even though defence is non-developmental.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Maintenance of existing assets is revenue expenditure.
2. Repayment of loans is capital expenditure.
3. Interest payments are capital expenditure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Maintenance and interest are revenue items; loan repayment changes liabilities, so it is capital.

s: The Plan and Non-plan classification of expenditure ended with which Union Budget?
x: The Plan/Non-plan split ended with Budget 2017-18, at the end of the 12th Plan; 2016-17 was the last Budget to use it.

s: Which committee (2011) called the Plan/Non-plan split of expenditure 'dysfunctional'?
x: The C. Rangarajan Committee (2011) called the split dysfunctional and an obstacle to outcome-based budgeting.

s: After the Plan/Non-plan split ended, how is Union expenditure mainly classified?
x: The Plan/Non-plan split was replaced by the revenue vs capital classification.

s: Which of the following was an item of non-plan expenditure of the Central Government?
x: Non-plan expenditure covered defence, interest payments and loans to States, UTs and PSUs.

s: Which approach to subsidies did the Sixteenth Finance Commission favour?
o: Well-targeted subsidies with exclusion criteria and sunset clauses
x: It supported well-targeted subsidies with exclusion criteria and sunset clauses, not unrestricted off-budget financing.

s: From which date was the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme introduced?
x: The Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme commenced on 1 April 2010.

s: Which fertiliser remains outside the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme?
x: NBS covers 22 grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers including DAP, MOP and SSP, with subsidy fixed per kg of nutrient; urea is outside the scheme.

s: Food and fertiliser subsidies together form about what share of the Union subsidy bill in 2026-27?
x: Food (₹2,27,629 crore) and fertiliser (₹1,70,799 crore) make up 87 per cent of the ₹4,54,773 crore subsidy bill.

s: Which of the following is an explicit subsidy?
x: Interest subvention appears as a budget line, so it is explicit; under-pricing of education, health and irrigation water are hidden subsidies.

s: Through which instrument were the under-recoveries of oil companies paid after the Oil Pool Account closed?
x: After the Oil Pool Account was closed on 1 April 2002, under-recoveries were paid through oil bonds.

s: Which of the following is a hidden (implicit) subsidy?
x: Hidden subsidies come from under-pricing public services like irrigation water; food, fertiliser and interest subvention are budget lines.

s: Under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme, a fixed subsidy is given per kg of which nutrients?
x: NBS gives a fixed subsidy per kg of nitrogen, phosphorus, potash and sulphur; urea is outside it.

s: Under which pricing system did the Oil Pool Account operate before it was closed on 1 April 2002?
x: The Oil Pool Account was part of the Administered Pricing Mechanism (APM), dismantled from 1 April 2002.

s: Which is the largest subsidy in the Union Budget 2026-27?
x: Food subsidy (₹2,27,629 crore) is the largest, followed by fertiliser (₹1,70,799 crore).

s: What is the total subsidy bill of the Union Government in Budget 2026-27?
x: Total subsidies are ₹4,54,773 crore; food and fertiliser make up 87%.

s: Major subsidies (food, fertiliser, petroleum) in 2026-27 are about what share of GDP?
x: Major subsidies of ₹4.11 lakh crore equal about 1.0% of GDP.

s: How many grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers are covered under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme?
x: NBS covers 22 grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers such as DAP, MOP and SSP; urea is outside it.

s: Who was the Union Finance Minister when the Oil Pool Account was closed on 1 April 2002?
x: The Oil Pool Account under the APM was closed on 1 April 2002, when Yashwant Sinha was Finance Minister.

s: Which of the following is a developmental expenditure?
x: Irrigation and flood control is developmental; defence, pensions and interest payments are non-developmental.

s: Which of the following is NOT a non-developmental expenditure?
x: Medical and public health is developmental expenditure; interest, pensions and administrative services are non-developmental.

s: Which of the following is a non-developmental expenditure?
x: Defence and border roads are non-developmental; rural development, power and railways are developmental.

s: Who chaired the Expenditure Management Commission of 2014?
x: Bimal Jalan chaired the 2014 Expenditure Management Commission and also, separately, the RBI Economic Capital Framework committee (2018-19).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Expenditure Reforms Commission was set up in February 2000 under K.P. Geethakrishnan; the Expenditure Management Commission (2014) was chaired by Bimal Jalan.

s: Who was the first President of the BRICS New Development Bank (2015)?
x: K.V. Kamath was the first President of the New Development Bank, not Bimal Jalan.

s: Who chaired the RBI committee on the Economic Capital Framework (2018-19)?
x: Bimal Jalan chaired the RBI Economic Capital Framework committee (2018-19) and the Expenditure Management Commission (2014).

s: For Indian States during 2014-24, revenue expenditure formed approximately what share of their total expenditure?
x: States' revenue expenditure was 80-87% of their total expenditure, while total State spending was 16.15-17.49% of GSDP in 2014-24. 50-55% and 60-65% understate the share; 92-97% overstates it.

s: In the Andhra Pradesh Budget Estimates for 2026-27, revenue expenditure constituted approximately what share of total expenditure?
x: Revenue expenditure constituted approximately 83% of Andhra Pradesh’s total expenditure in the 2026-27 Budget Estimates.

s: During 2014-24, total expenditure of the States was in which range of GSDP?
x: States spent 16.15-17.49% of GSDP during 2014-24, with revenue expenditure 80-87% of the total.

s: In the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27, which is the correct order of expenditure by size?
o: Capital outlay > Revenue expenditure > Loans and advances
Revenue expenditure > Loans and advances > Capital outlay
Revenue expenditure > Capital outlay > Loans and advances
Loans and advances > Capital outlay > Revenue expenditure
x: AP spends most on revenue expenditure (about 83 per cent), then capital outlay, then loans and advances.

s: About how much is Andhra Pradesh's capital outlay in Budget Estimates 2026-27?
x: AP's capital outlay is ₹48,698 crore (+47 per cent) in BE 2026-27; ₹33,135 crore was 2025-26 RE and ₹16,141 crore 2024-25.

s: Which of the following correctly defines effective capital expenditure?
o: Capital expenditure plus grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets
Revenue expenditure plus loans to State Governments
Capital expenditure minus grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets
Capital outlay plus interest payments on public debt
x: Effective capital expenditure is calculated as capital expenditure plus grants-in-aid for the creation of capital assets.

s: What does the Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) provide to States?
x: SASCI provides 50-year interest-free loans to States for capital expenditure.

s: What does the Union capital expenditure of ₹12,21,821 crore in Budget 2026-27 consist of?
o: Capital outlay plus loans and advances
Capital outlay plus grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets
Revenue expenditure plus loans and advances
x: Capex 2026-27 (₹12,21,821 crore, +11.5%) = capital outlay ₹9,43,042 crore + loans ₹2,78,780 crore. Adding grants-in-aid for capital assets gives effective capex, not capex. Revenue expenditure and interest payments are not part of capital expenditure.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about effective capital expenditure in BE 2026-27?
o: Grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets account for ₹4.93 lakh crore of it
It is estimated at 101.1 per cent of the fiscal deficit
Grants to States are revenue expenditure even when used to create assets
It excludes grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets
x: Effective capital expenditure includes grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets.

s: What is the Union's effective capital expenditure in Budget Estimates 2026-27?
x: Effective capex = capex ₹12.22 lakh crore + grants for capital assets ₹4.93 lakh crore = ₹17.15 lakh crore.

s: Effective capital expenditure in BE 2026-27 is about what share of GDP?
x: Effective capex of ₹17.15 lakh crore is 4.4% of GDP; plain capex is 3.1%.

s: Union capital expenditure in Budget 2026-27 is about what share of GDP?
x: Capex of ₹12,21,821 crore (+11.5%) is 3.1% of GDP.

s: What does Wagner's law state about public expenditure as an economy industrialises?
o: Public expenditure rises faster than national income
Public expenditure falls faster than national income
Public expenditure rises only during wars and crises
Public expenditure remains constant irrespective of national income
x: Wagner’s law, also called the law of increasing state activity, holds that public expenditure rises faster than national income as an economy industrialises.

s: With which of the following is the displacement effect in public expenditure theory associated?
o: The fiscal multiplier of capital expenditure
x: The displacement effect is associated with the Peacock-Wiseman hypothesis. Wars and crises raise the tolerable tax burden and displace public spending to a higher level.

s: The Peacock-Wiseman hypothesis was based on public expenditure data of which country?
x: Peacock and Wiseman (1961) studied UK data and found spending rises in steps (displacement effect).

s: Wagner's law is also known as the law of what?
x: Wagner's law, that spending rises faster than national income as an economy industrialises, is the law of increasing state activity.

s: In which year did Peacock and Wiseman put forward their hypothesis on public expenditure growth?
x: Peacock and Wiseman (1961) used UK data to show spending rises in steps (displacement effect).

s: Who owes most of India's external debt?
o: Non-sovereign borrowers such as companies and banks
x: Most external debt is non-sovereign; the Government's external debt is only about 2.6% of GDP.

s: Which institution publishes ‘India's External Debt: A Status Report’?
o: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
x: The report is published by the Department of Economic Affairs under the Ministry of Finance. The RBI compiles the quarterly external-debt data.

s: Which currency had the largest share in India's external debt at end-December 2025?
x: The US dollar had 54.8 per cent, the rupee 30.1 per cent and the yen 6.3 per cent - not all debt is in dollars.

s: Which is the largest multilateral lender in India's external debt?
x: The Asian Development Bank is the largest multilateral lender with 32.8 per cent.

s: India's external debt at end-December 2025 was about what share of GDP?
x: India's external debt was USD 765.5 billion, about 20.4 per cent of GDP, at end-December 2025. The 2.6 per cent figure is only the government's own external debt.

s: Which was the largest component of India's external debt at end-December 2025?
x: Commercial borrowings have long been the largest component of India's external debt and were still the largest at end-December 2025.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the classification of the Union Government's liabilities?
o: Loans from foreign governments — Internal debt
x: Small savings and post-office deposits are other liabilities recorded in the Public Account. Market loans are internal debt, while loans from foreign governments are external debt.

s: Internal debt constitutes what share of India's public debt?
x: Internal debt is 96.7% of public debt; G-Secs are over 90% of Central Government debt.

s: On what basis is public debt classified into internal and external debt?
x: Internal and external debt are distinguished by where the government borrows from.

s: What are short-term government debt instruments called?
x: Treasury Bills are short-term; G-Secs are long-term and SDLs are issued by States.

s:
Consider the following statements about Internal Debt:
I. Its source is the domestic economy.
II. Its key idea is domestic borrowing.
III. It may involve foreign-denominated obligations.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: I and II are correct: internal debt is borrowed within the country. III is false because foreign-currency obligations belong to external debt.

s: Which pair consists only of instruments of internal debt?
x: G-Secs and Treasury Bills are internal-debt instruments; external assistance and foreign borrowings are external debt.

s: Special securities issued to the National Small Savings Fund form part of which of the following?
x: NSSF securities, like saving and compensation bonds and 14-day intermediate T-Bills, are non-marketable internal debt.

s: Under Article 292 of the Constitution, against which fund are borrowings forming the Public Debt of the Union contracted?
x: Article 292 relates to borrowings by the Government of India against the security of the Consolidated Fund of India. Other liabilities are recorded in the Public Account.

s: Which is the main account of the Government of India?
x: The Consolidated Fund is the main account and receives loan recoveries; the Public Account holds trust money.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government must repay or use money in the Public Account of India according to applicable rules.
2. The Contingency Fund of India is the main account into which government revenues are credited.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Public Account money is held in trust and repaid or used by rule. The main government account is the Consolidated Fund, not the Contingency Fund.

s: In which account is money held by the Government of India in trust kept?
x: The Public Account holds money in trust. The Consolidated Fund is the main account, the Contingency Fund meets urgent needs and the NIF has a permanent corpus.

s: Which of the following is a non-marketable instrument of the Centre's internal debt?
x: NSSF special securities are non-marketable internal debt; G-Secs, T-Bills and Cash Management Bills are marketable.

s: Provident Fund is an example of which type of savings?
x: Provident Fund is contractual savings: a fixed part of salary is saved under a contract. It is an 'other liability' of the Centre.

s: Government securities (G-Secs) make up roughly what share of the Central Government's debt?
x: G-Secs (dated market loans) form over 90% of Central debt, and internal debt is 96.7% of public debt.

s: Through which of the following do household bank deposits mainly reach government borrowing?
x: Bank deposits flow to government borrowing through SLR holdings, alongside small savings/NSSF and insurance and provident funds.

s: Market borrowings are the largest source of which of the following?
x: Market borrowings are the biggest source of the government's capital receipts.

s: What is the gross market borrowing of the Centre budgeted for 2026-27?
x: Gross market borrowing is ₹17.20 lakh crore in 2026-27; net borrowing is ₹11.73 lakh crore.

s: What is the Centre's new medium-term debt-GDP target?
x: The new medium-term target is to bring the Centre’s debt-GDP ratio to 50 ± 1% by 31 March 2031.

s: What debt target for the Centre for 2024-25 was set by the FRBM Act, as amended in 2018?
x: General government debt was set at 60% with the Centre at 40%, as the N.K. Singh Committee recommended (States 20%).

s: Which change was made in Budget 2026-27 regarding the principal fiscal anchor?
o: Revenue deficit replaced the primary balance.
The current account deficit replaced public debt.
The fiscal deficit replaced the debt-GDP ratio.
The debt-GDP ratio replaced the fiscal deficit.
x: Budget 2026-27 made the debt-GDP ratio the primary target instead of the fiscal deficit.

s:
Consider the following statements about the FRBM (2018) debt targets:
1. General government debt target is 60 per cent of GDP.
2. The Centre's share of it is 40 per cent and the States' 20 per cent.
3. They followed the N.K. Singh Committee (2017).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The FRBM (2018), following the N.K. Singh Committee (2017), set general government debt at 60 per cent: Centre 40 and States 20.

s: What is the Centre's debt-GDP ratio in the Budget Estimates 2026-27?
x: The Centre's debt-GDP is 55.6 per cent in BE 2026-27; it peaked at 61 per cent in 2020-21.

s: In which year did the Centre's debt-GDP ratio reach its peak of about 61%?
x: Central debt peaked at about 61% of GDP in the pandemic year 2020-21; it is 55.6% in BE 2026-27.

s: Which pair of indicators is especially relevant for assessing the debt sustainability of States?
o: Debt-GSDP ratio and interest payments-to-revenue receipts ratio
Current account deficit and foreign exchange reserves
Fiscal deficit-to-GDP ratio and export-import ratio
x: For States, debt-GSDP and interest payments as a proportion of revenue receipts are the key sustainability ratios.

s: Since 2005-06, how have external loans to States been raised?
x: External loans reach States only through the Centre, on a back-to-back basis for general category States.

s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission has capped the fiscal deficit of States at what percentage of GSDP for 2026-31?
x: The fiscal deficit of States has been capped at 3% of GSDP for 2026-31 under the Sixteenth Finance Commission framework.

s: Which State had the highest debt or outstanding liabilities as a percentage of GSDP among the following in 2023-24?
x: Punjab had the highest ratio among the listed States at 42.9% of GSDP in 2023-24, followed by West Bengal at 38.3%, Rajasthan at 37.9% and Andhra Pradesh at 34.6%.

s: Under Article 293 of the Constitution, how may a State Government borrow?
o: Only within the territory of India, upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of the State
From anywhere, including abroad, upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of India
Only from the Reserve Bank of India, without any security
Only from foreign governments, with the consent of Parliament
x: Article 293 allows States to borrow only within India on the security of the State's Consolidated Fund; they do so by issuing State Development Loans (SDLs). States cannot borrow abroad directly (external loans come through the Centre since 2005-06), are not restricted to the RBI, and do not borrow from foreign governments directly.

s: According to the 2025-26 Revised Estimates, what was the total debt of Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's total debt in 2025-26 RE was ₹6,35,177 crore = 36.04% of GSDP (35.73% in 2024-25), with market borrowing (₹4,83,093 crore) the largest component. ₹5,64,488 crore/35.15% is the 2024-25 RE figure; ₹9,74,556 crore is total liabilities incl. PSUs (White Paper); 42.9% is Punjab's ratio and ₹4,83,093 crore is only the market-borrowing part.

s: Through which instrument do States mainly raise market borrowings?
x: Under Article 293 States borrow only within India, through State Development Loans (SDLs).

s: Which is the largest component of Andhra Pradesh's outstanding debt (2025-26 RE)?
x: Of AP's total debt of Rs 6,35,177 crore (2025-26 RE), market borrowing of Rs 4,83,093 crore is the largest part.

s: What did the 16th Finance Commission recommend about off-budget borrowing?
o: Stopped, with existing off-budget debt brought on-budget
x: The 16th FC recommended stopping off-budget borrowing, bringing existing debt on-budget and widening the definitions of deficit and debt.

s: The main concern about State off-budget borrowings and guarantees is that they:
o: Make consolidated public debt appear lower than it actually is
x: Off-budget borrowings and guarantees conceal the true consolidated debt burden and may weigh on sovereign ratings.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about public debt management in India?
o: The PDMC was set up in 2016 in the Department of Economic Affairs
A statutory PDMA was first proposed in Budget 2015-16
The PDMC is headed by the Joint Secretary (Budget)
The statutory PDMA has been created and has taken over the RBI's Public Debt Office
x: The statutory PDMA has not yet been created; the RBI still manages public debt.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Reserve Bank of India – Banker to the Centre and States under the RBI Act, 1934
Public Debt Management Cell – Set up in 2016 within the RBI
Public Debt Office – Issue, servicing and records of G-Secs
Department of Economic Affairs – Debt strategy and external borrowing
x: The PDMC was set up in 2016 in the Department of Economic Affairs, headed by the Joint Secretary (Budget), not within the RBI.

s: At what share of GDP a year does the FRBM framework cap new Central government guarantees?
x: New Central guarantees, treated as contingent liabilities, are capped at 0.5% of GDP a year.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about off-budget borrowing?
o: The Food Corporation of India borrowed from the NSSF to cover unpaid food subsidy
Budget 2021-22 ended the FCI-NSSF arrangement and brought food subsidy on-budget
Loans raised by government entities and serviced from the budget are counted in the fiscal deficit
Off-budget borrowing hides the true level of debt
x: Off-budget loans are serviced from the budget but are kept outside the fiscal deficit - that is why they are called off-budget. The other statements are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about public debt management:
1. The RBI manages government debt under the RBI Act, 1934.
2. A statutory Public Debt Management Agency was set up after the 2015-16 Budget.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The RBI manages debt under the RBI Act, 1934. The statutory PDMA was proposed in 2015-16 but not created.

s: What was the off-budget borrowing of Andhra Pradesh in March 2023?
x: AP's off-budget borrowing was ₹1.28 lakh crore (9.7 per cent of GSDP) in March 2023.

s: If the primary deficit is zero, fresh government borrowing is needed only for which of the following?
x: Primary deficit excludes interest payments; when it is zero, fresh borrowing covers only interest.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the interest-growth differential?
o: When r exceeds g, a primary surplus is needed
The differential is r − g, where g is nominal GDP growth
When g exceeds r, the debt-GDP ratio can fall even with a small primary deficit
When the effective interest rate exceeds nominal GDP growth, the debt-GDP ratio falls even with a primary deficit
x: When r exceeds g, a primary surplus is needed to stabilise debt; the ratio does not fall with a primary deficit.

s: Interest payments on Central debt are approximately what proportion of revenue receipts?
x: Interest payments account for about 40% of revenue receipts, thereby limiting the fiscal space for other expenditure.

s: Public debt has become a fiscal anchor mainly because high interest payments:
o: Squeeze expenditure on other public purposes
Expand fiscal space for capital expenditure
x: Interest payments of about 40% of revenue receipts constrain fiscal space and squeeze other spending.

s: If the interest rate (r) exceeds the growth rate (g), what is required to keep the debt-GDP ratio stable?
x: When r > g, a primary surplus is needed; when g > r, the debt-GDP ratio falls on its own.

s: What is meant by a 'debt trap'?
o: Borrowing to pay interest on past debt
Repaying debt out of a revenue surplus
x: A debt trap arises when a government borrows just to pay interest on its past debt, so debt keeps growing.

s: In Indian usage, how is the budget gap met under deficit financing?
o: Borrowing from the RBI, which creates new money
x: In India, deficit financing means borrowing from the RBI and creating new money; Western usage covers any financing of a deficit.

s: What does deficit financing mean in Western usage?
o: Only borrowing from the central bank
Any financing of a budget deficit, mainly by borrowing from the public
Printing currency to pay for imports
x: In the West it means any financing of a budget deficit, mainly market borrowing; in India it means borrowing from the RBI.

s: What is the effect of deficit financing through borrowing from the RBI on the money supply?
o: It leaves the money supply unchanged
It turns the money supply into foreign exchange
x: When the RBI lends to the government it creates new money, so money supply rises; that is why deficit financing is inflationary.

s: In the Union Budget, what does the fiscal deficit equal?
o: Budgetary deficit plus net increase in internal and external borrowings and other liabilities
x: Fiscal deficit = budgetary deficit + net increase in internal and external borrowings and other liabilities.

s: In India, deficit financing was used as a pragmatic tool mainly to finance which of the following?
x: Deficit financing mobilised resources for economic development and financed the Five Year Plans.

s: India's reliance on deficit financing became heavier from which period onwards?
x: Deficit financing was used in a limited way until the late 1960s and relied on more heavily from the 1970s onwards.

s: Which one of the following was NOT identified as a major reason for the need for deficit financing in India after Independence?
o: Low tax base and poor tax compliance
x: The post-Independence need arose partly because India had a low tax base, poor compliance, a weak privately owned banking sector and low domestic savings. An excessively high savings rate was not a reason.

s: How much was deficit financing in the Second Five Year Plan?
x: Deficit financing in the Second Plan was about ₹1,100 crore against ₹1,200 crore planned.

s: In which Five Year Plan was reliance on deficit financing to be strictly limited?
x: The Third Plan said reliance on deficit financing would be strictly limited.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the effect of RBI open market operations?
o: Sale of Government securities injects liquidity and purchase absorbs liquidity
Sale of Government securities absorbs liquidity and purchase injects liquidity
Both sale and purchase absorb liquidity
Neither sale nor purchase affects liquidity
x: Through OMOs, sale of Government securities absorbs liquidity from the system, while purchase of securities injects liquidity.

s: For what purpose were ad hoc Treasury Bills, now abolished, used?
o: Automatic RBI financing of the government
x: Ad hoc Treasury Bills gave automatic RBI financing to the government; they were replaced by Ways and Means Advances.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about methods of deficit financing?
o: Borrowing from the RBI monetises the deficit
Ways and Means Advances are temporary advances from the RBI
An OMO sale of G-Secs adds liquidity
Ad hoc Treasury Bills have been abolished
x: An OMO sale of G-Secs drains liquidity; a purchase adds it. The other statements are correct.

s: On 15 September 2026, the RBI announced open market operation (OMO) sales of how much?
x: On 15 September 2026 the RBI announced OMO sales of ₹1 lakh crore; an OMO sale drains liquidity.

s: When the FRBM escape clause is invoked, what is the cap on deviation from the fiscal target?
x: The escape-clause deviation is capped at 0.5% of GDP a year; since 2018 monetised borrowing is allowed only on escape-clause grounds.

s: From which date did Ways and Means Advances (WMA) come into operation?
x: WMA began on 1 April 1997 after the March 1997 agreement ended ad hoc T-bills, whose phase-out began in September 1994.

s: When was the RBI-Government agreement that began phasing out ad hoc Treasury Bills signed?
x: The September 1994 agreement began the phase-out; the March 1997 agreement ended ad hoc T-bills.

s: From which date was the RBI barred from subscribing to primary issues of government securities?
x: Under the FRBM framework the RBI was barred from primary issues from 1 April 2006, though the FRBM Act is of 2003.

s: Since the 2018 FRBM amendment, under which condition is monetised borrowing from the RBI allowed?
o: Up to 3 per cent of GDP
x: Since 2018 monetised borrowing is allowed only on escape-clause grounds, with the slip capped at 0.5 per cent of GDP.

s: Which of the following is NOT inflationary in its effect?
x: Repayment of debt withdraws money from the economy, so it is not inflationary; creation of new money is the most inflationary.

s: In Indian public finance, how is a government financing gap covered under deficit financing?
o: Drawing down cash balances, borrowing from the RBI or issuing new currency
Transferring revenue receipts to the central bank
x: Deficit financing in the Indian context includes drawing down cash balances, borrowing from the RBI and issuing new currency to cover the financing gap.

s: Which route of deficit financing is the most inflationary?
x: Money creation through RBI borrowing is the most inflationary route; public borrowing absorbs liquidity.

s: Which of the following is part of the Centre's 'other liabilities' and not internal debt?
x: State Provident Funds sit in the Public Account as other liabilities; market loans, T-Bills and NSSF securities are internal debt.

s: Market loans make up about what share of Andhra Pradesh's debt?
x: Market loans are about 75 per cent of AP's debt.

s: What is heavy government market borrowing that raises interest rates and squeezes private investment called?
x: Absorbing loanable funds and squeezing private investment is crowding out; borrowing to pay interest is the debt trap.

s: Deficit financing is particularly likely to cause demand-pull inflation when it:
o: Uses existing savings without increasing aggregate demand
Raises money supply and demand without a corresponding increase in goods and services
Withdraws money through repayment of public debt
x: RBI financing can raise money supply and demand without a matching increase in goods and services, producing demand-pull inflation. The burden of such inflation tends to affect the poor most severely.

s: What was the fiscal deficit of Andhra Pradesh in 2024–25?
x: AP's 2024–25 fiscal deficit of 5.05 per cent exceeded the 4 per cent ceiling; market loans form 75 per cent of its debt.

s: The Reserve Bank of India has urged governments to shift the emphasis in expenditure from which item to which?
x: The RBI has urged a shift from subsidies towards capital expenditure, or capex.

s: How much of every rupee spent in Union Budget 2026-27 goes to interest payments?
x: Interest takes 20 paise of every rupee spent, about 40 per cent of revenue receipts.

s: Which consequence of deficit financing refers to borrowing merely to pay interest on past loans?
x: A debt trap is borrowing to pay interest on old loans; it leaves little money for health and education.

s: States had borrowed Rs 5.23 trillion up to October 2025. About what share of their FY26 borrowing plan was this?
x: States borrowed Rs 5.23 trillion till October 2025, about 62% of their FY26 plan.

s: Which of the following does Andhra Pradesh currently run?
x: AP still runs a primary deficit, so it has a fiscal deficit even after excluding interest payments.

s: With reference to Union Government deficits, which one of the following correctly represents the fiscal deficit in 2020-21 and 2026-27 (BE), respectively?
x: The fiscal deficit was 9.2% of GDP in 2020-21, the peak shown in the series, and is estimated at 4.3% in 2026-27 (BE).

s: To what per cent of GDP did India's fiscal deficit decline from 9.2 per cent during its fiscal consolidation?
x: The decline from 9.2 to 4.4 per cent was linked to three sovereign rating upgrades in 2025 by Morningstar DBRS, S&P and R&I.

s: What was the Union fiscal deficit in 2021-22?
